question.worked_solution:
Recall that the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $z$-axis is given by

$$
z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

Thus, a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $O$ whose axis of symmetry is the $x$**-axis** is given by

$$
x=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, our equation is a hyperbolic paraboloid whose axis of symmetry is the $x$-axis and $b=2\sqrt{2},\,c=3.$
